issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor implementation in the solution swaps the constructor parameter names/roles compared to the template/header. In the template the constructor is defined as Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) and initializes width(p_width), height(p_height). In the solution the implementation is Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_height, int p_width) and initializes width(p_width), height(p_height) — i.e. the first parameter is treated as height and the second as width in the initializer. This is a semantic mismatch with the header declaration (Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height)) and with the template implementation, and can cause incorrect width/height assignment at runtime and confuse students comparing template and solution code.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution implementation match the header and the template by using the same parameter ordering and initializer. Change the solution constructor to: Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) : width(p_width), height(p_height) { ... } (or, alternatively, update the header to match the intended parameter order, but keeping header and implementation consistent is required). This resolves the semantic mismatch and avoids confusing students.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor's parameter names/order differ between the header/template and the solution implementation. The header (and template implementation) declare/define the ctor as width then height (e.g. Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) / Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height)) while the solution's implementation uses the parameters in reversed positions (Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_height, int p_width)) and initializes members as width(p_width), height(p_height). This mismatch effectively swaps width and height when the ctor is called with (width, height) and creates a semantic discrepancy between template, header and solution that will confuse students mapping the API declaration to the provided solution code (and may cause incorrect behavior).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution implementation match the header/template naming and ordering. For example change the solution constructor to: Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) : width(i_width), height(i_height) { } — or, if keeping the parameter names p_width/p_height, ensure their order and member initialization correspond to the header (first parameter = width, second = height). This ensures a consistent mapping between declaration, template and solution and avoids swapped width/height semantics.
